topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Electric circuits, current and potential difference
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: series/parallel voltage and current; TGS 2026-27: Electricity 2
topic.overview: Circuit behaviour can be predicted using charge flow and energy transfer. Current describes charge flow, while potential difference describes energy transferred per unit charge.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge and is measured in amperes (A).
An ammeter is connected in series with the component or branch being measured.
Potential difference is energy transferred per unit charge and is measured in volts (V).
A voltmeter is connected in parallel across a component.
A complete conducting loop is needed for sustained current.
Current is the same everywhere in a simple series circuit.
At a junction, total current entering equals total current leaving.
Potential differences across series components add to the supply; parallel branches have the same potential difference as the supply.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: unit of potential difference, symbol V
instrument connected in series to measure current
instrument connected in parallel to measure potential difference

workedExamples.prompt: 0.6 A reaches a junction and 0.2 A enters one branch. Find the other branch current.
A 9 V supply has series components with 3 V and an unknown p.d. Find it.

practicals.title: Current and p.d. in series and parallel
practicals.aim: Measure current and potential difference in contrasting circuits.
practicals.variables: IV: arrangement or number of components; DV: current/p.d.; controls: component type, supply setting and temperature.
practicals.method: Build with the supply off, place ammeters in series and voltmeters across components, switch on briefly, record and repeat for series and parallel arrangements.
practicals.expectedResult: Series current is unchanged around a loop; branch currents add; series p.d.s add and parallel branch p.d.s match the supply.
practicals.safety: Use a low-voltage supply, check for short circuits and switch off if components become hot.
practicals.evaluation: Use correct meter range and polarity, repeat readings and account for component heating.

commonMistakes: Connecting an ammeter across a component.
Saying current is used up by a lamp.
examTips: Current goes through: ammeter in series.
Potential difference is across: voltmeter in parallel.
Mark every junction before applying current conservation.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.topic: Electric circuits, current and potential difference
practicals.title: Current and p.d. in series and parallel
practicals.aim: Measure current and potential difference in contrasting circuits.
practicals.variables: IV: arrangement or number of components; DV: current/p.d.; controls: component type, supply setting and temperature.
practicals.method: Build with the supply off, place ammeters in series and voltmeters across components, switch on briefly, record and repeat for series and parallel arrangements.
practicals.expectedResult: Series current is unchanged around a loop; branch currents add; series p.d.s add and parallel branch p.d.s match the supply.
practicals.safety: Use a low-voltage supply, check for short circuits and switch off if components become hot.
practicals.evaluation: Use correct meter range and polarity, repeat readings and account for component heating.
